newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says squatter demolition a last resort.
newsitem.headline: Manila says squatter demolition a last resort.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos, under fire over squatter clearances ahead of next month's APEC summit, said on Friday the demolitions would go on.
But he said they would only occur when all other means of trying to persuade squatters to move had failed.
"Demolition is not the normal policy of dealing with our poor," Ramos said in a speech at a ceremony inaugurating a housing project for the poor.

Church groups and others have attacked Ramos over the demolitions, accusing his government of cleaning up the capital ahead of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting at the expense of the poor.

Ramos said in his speech that the demolitions would continue but only when "negotiations and dialogue fail, and demolitions are necessary for the common good, especially in danger zones and in sites of urgent government infrastructure projects".
Many squatters live along river banks prone to flooding and along national highways that are being improved.
